findings.title: Ledger worked example recomputes the credit from a backed-out fee instead of showing the listed credit, so it is off by one cent for any odd-cent entry
findings.failurePath: LedgerScreen.example works out fee = amountCents*100 ~/ 40, then prints formatCents(fee*40 ~/ 100) as the result and calls it 'its credit below'. That only works back exactly when amountCents is even, and nothing enforces that: FeeEntry has no assert, and the only safeguard is a doc comment ('Seeded credits are even cents'). feeEntries is a public ValueNotifier, and the ledger rebuilds on every change and always uses entries.first. If the newest entry is 1241 cents, the example reads 'traders paid $31.02 in fees. 40% of $31.02 = $12.40, its credit below', while the row below shows $12.41. A 1-cent entry gives a $0.02 fee and a $0.00 credit against a listed $0.01. A negative entry of -1241 gives -$12.40 against a listed -$12.41, because ~/ truncates toward zero. Today's seed (1240, 860, 1016, 640, 524) is all even, so the shipped app and the current test do not hit this. It breaks as soon as a seed edit or the planned phase-7 derivation adds an odd-cent credit.
findings.fix: Make the example's right-hand side the listed credit, formatCents(e.amountCents), so the equality cannot drift. Or seed the fee traders paid (feeCents) and derive amountCents = feeCents * 40 ~/ 100 forward, so the 40% share is the real computation, using the same floor rule as phase 2's fee. Either way, add one test with an odd-cent entry.
findings.evidence: Read receipt_screens.dart:63-71 and market_mock.dart, where YourMarketMock.fees seeds 1240/860/1016/640/524. Ran a scratch Dart check of the same expressions: 1241 -> fee 3102 -> credit 1240; 1 -> fee 2 -> credit 0; -1241 -> fee -3102 -> credit -1240; all five seeds round-trip exactly. Checked receipts_test.dart:171-184: it asserts the example only against the even seed.

checked: Scope: both refs resolve (phase-6 5fd70c1, phase-5 9bf4364). The three-dot diff lists 56 files, 10 of them under app/lib. The worktree HEAD is 5fd70c1 on feat/br-2026-10-04-p0-queue/phase-6. Commits in range, newest first: 5fd70c1, ef02185, 63c6002 (the feature commit), 09ae74d.

Every fee amount is an int in cents from seed to display. FeeEntry.amountCents is int and the seed values are int literals. Scenario.marketFeesCents is a fold over int starting at 0. Display goes through the phase-2 formatCents(int). Grepping the app/lib diff for double, toDouble, .round(), num, toStringAsFixed and '/ ' found no new double on the money path.

Totals are computed from the entries when the widget builds; nothing stores a total. The stored $42.80 constants (PortfolioMock.fees, YourMarketMock.feesThisWeek) are deleted. The Wallet row (portfolio_screen.dart _feesLine), the Your market chip (your_market_screen.dart) and the Ledger footer all render formatCents(Scenario.marketFeesCents) inside a ListenableBuilder on Listenable.merge([feeEntries, marketId]), so all three show the same value and update when an entry changes. receipts_test 'ledger total equals the sum of listed entries' drops an entry and checks that both the ledger and the Wallet row follow.

The Ledger footer and the listed rows use the same filter (Scenario.marketFees, entries whose marketId equals marketId.value) in the same synchronous build, so the footer always equals the sum of the rows shown.

Leaving out credits for other markets is intended scoping, not a silent drop. If the user lists under a ticker other than MAYA, the ledger says 'No fee credits yet' and shows $0.00, which the test 'a market with no credits shows an empty ledger and zero' covers. The seed contains only MAYA entries.

The 40% arithmetic is integer-only (~/). Its floor rounding matches phase 2's fee rule (scenario.dart:364, feeCents = notionalCents * feeBps ~/ 10000). Phase 2's margin uses .round() on a double, but that is a different quantity.

The 40% share is labelled a demo assumption in all three places: the ledger header 'Illustrative demo ledger · 40% share is a demo assumption', the worked example (it uses $pct%), and the make_market_flow line 'You earn 40% of the fees from both' with YourMarketMock.shareLabel under it. All are derived from the single const creatorSharePct = 40.
formatCents handles negative amounts (Unicode minus sign before the $) and zero ($0.00). The no-credits path renders formatCents(0).
CallReceipt.entryPrice is String? and documented as a fixed-decimal string, so no new double price type. No seeded call states one, so it always renders 'unavailable'.
Overflow: the sums are 5 small ints, and the example's amountCents*100 stays under 2^53 on web up to about 9e13 cents. No real int64 or 2^53 risk in this diff.
reset() restores feeEntries and callReceipts to the identical seed lists (receipts_test checks this with same()).
make_market_flow's 'VistaType.bodyStrong.copyWith(fontSize: 14)' predates this phase (the diff only moves it into a Column), so it is not new in this diff.

findings.title: Call details tells the user 'No call in fixture-v1 backs this holding' for maya.eth's SOL long, but fixture-v1 has that exact call
findings.failurePath: Home feed -> caller maya.eth -> ProfileScreen('maya.eth') -> HOLDING NOW -> tap the SOL (Long 5x) row. forHolding('maya.eth', SOL long) skips the seeded receipt 'maya-sol-300-fri' (author maya.eth, asset SOL, side long) only because its result is CallOutcome.right, not open. It falls through to the synthetic CallReceipt(id:'none'), whose null rule picks the header 'No call in fixture-v1 backs this holding', plus 7 'unavailable' rows. Back on the same screen, 'All receipts ›' lists 'SOL reaches $300 by Fri - Right' by maya.eth, and the CALLS sample right under the holdings shows the same call. The receipt screen makes a false statement about the fixture. The same path applies through ProfileScreen(maya.eth) -> market -> Portfolio panel -> SOL. receipts_test.dart only checks maya's ETH and BTC rows on her own profile, so nothing catches this.
findings.fix: Either make the copy true ('No open call in fixture-v1 backs this holding'), or have forHolding fall back to the newest settled call by the same author on the same asset and side when no open one exists. Add a SOL assertion to 'each record item opens its call receipt' for whichever rule is chosen.
findings.evidence: Read forHolding (the result == CallOutcome.open filter), the market_mock.dart record seed (maya-sol-300-fri: SOL, TradeSide.long, CallOutcome.right), ProfileMock.holdings (SOL long 5x), profile_screen.dart:93-99 (HoldingsTable -> forHolding(widget.handle, h)), and ProfileScreen.route reachable for 'maya.eth' from home_screen.dart:113 via mock_trade_idea callerHandle 'maya.eth'. Checked receipts_test.dart:225-258: there is no SOL assertion for maya.eth.

findings.title: The made-up 'unavailable' receipt still says Provenance fixture-v1, which contradicts its own header
findings.location: app/lib/features/market/receipt_screens.dart:281-283 with market_mock.dart CallReceipt default provenance = Scenario.fixtureVersion
findings.failurePath: ProfileScreen('maya.eth') -> HOLDING NOW -> BTC row (or any holding on kaito.eth's profile or trader market). The screen header says 'No call in fixture-v1 backs this holding', then the Provenance row says 'fixture-v1' in strong type, next to Author and Asset. The page reads as a receipt sourced from the fixture for a call the fixture does not contain. The test expects exactly 7 'unavailable' rows, which locks in this provenance line.
findings.fix: Build the fallback receipt with a provenance that says what it is (for example 'none: no fixture-v1 call'). Or make provenance nullable for the synthetic case so it renders 'unavailable', and update the findsNWidgets(7) count.
findings.evidence: Read the CallReceipt constructor default (this.provenance = Scenario.fixtureVersion), forHolding's fallback CallReceipt(id: 'none', author, asset), the CallReceiptScreen fields list ('Provenance', r.provenance), and receipts_test.dart:239-241.

findings.title: Confirmed iter-1 L6: a market listed seconds ago already shows $42.80 'earned in fees this week', all dated before it existed
findings.location: app/lib/scenario/scenario.dart:111-118 (marketFees filters only on marketId) with market_mock.dart:124-140 (seed dated chartEnd minus 3h to 96h)
findings.failurePath: Default start (no HAS_MARKET) -> Portfolio -> make-a-market flow -> keep the suggested ticker MAYA -> list. AccountState.listMarket sets Scenario.marketId to 'MAYA'. The Wallet row 'Fees from your market' jumps to $42.80, and the Ledger lists five credits for Tue 22 Sep to Sat 26 Sep (11:45), before the listing at Scenario.clock 26 Sep 14:45. The 'Illustrative demo ledger' line only appears inside the ledger. The Wallet row and the Your market chip carry no label and read as real income earned before the market existed.
findings.fix: In the no-market start, filter credits to those at or after the listing time (store the listing instant in Scenario at listMarket), or seed credits relative to listing. Or put an 'illustrative' cue on the Wallet row and chip. Low priority: the pre-phase constant had the same total.
findings.evidence: Traced AccountState.listMarket -> Scenario.marketId.value = symbol. Scenario.ticker is seeded to PortfolioMock.marketSymbol 'MAYA'. Fee seed times computed with python from TradeMock.chartEnd = 2026-09-26 14:45. Portfolio _fees row shows only when hasMarket.

reset() reassigns feeEntries = YourMarketMock.fees (List.unmodifiable) and callReceipts = YourMarketMock.record (const list). Nothing in lib mutates either notifier, so reset restores the identical seed object every time, which is deeper than deep equality.
